note:
The coach standing, ITS TWO LAMPS FLICKERING. Written at 2x the drawn height per R5a -- it had been stored at 1.00x, every stored pixel a screen pixel with no resampling, so it read visibly crisper than Thad at 2.19x and Hob at 5.93x and looked pasted into the room.

THE LAMPS ARE FOUND, NOT ASSUMED: the two brightest warm cores in the BODY's left 55% -- 363px at x630 and 274px at x196, both at y261, which is lamps mounted either side of the door. A first attempt caught 44 'flames' because brass fittings and horse highlights are also bright and warm; measuring in the body and taking the top two found the real pair.

Multiplies only those flames and a soft halo, never the sprite, which would pulse the coachwork. Irregular -- 1.00, 1.07, 0.95, 1.05, 0.97, 1.02 -- and shallower than Hob's, because two lamps on a standing body read steadier than one lantern in a hand.

AND THE HORSES ARE ALIVE, over 24 frames:

  the FAR head nods    period 6, curve 0 -3 -5 -4 -1 +1
  the NEAR head nods   period 6, the same curve offset two frames -- it leads
  the TAILS swish      period 6, horizontally
  the DRIVER'S HANDS   PERIOD 8, so they never lock to the horses
  the LAMPS flicker    period 6

6 and 8 are coprime, so the hands and the animals realign only every 24 frames and never read as one machine. That is why the clip is 24 rather than 6.

THE WHOLE-MASS WEIGHT SHIFT IS REMOVED. A head nod and a body shift together read as a horse dry-heaving -- the head goes down while the body comes up, which is what retching looks like. The head alone reads as breathing.

Every mask FEATHERED, all offsets in source pixels so about half that on screen. Despilled per frame, because shifting pulls edge pixels inward.

STORED AT 1.15x THE DRAWN HEIGHT, NOT 2x. R5a's 2x is right for a character; applied to a 956-wide coach across 24 frames it produced 26MB a clip and 70MB across the three, in the REQUIRED boot set because beat 2 stages it -- which is the exact problem R5a was written to prevent. 1.15x is still RESAMPLED at draw time, which was the whole reason 1.00x read wrong, at a third of the pixels.
